newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged to up 1/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged to up 1/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal cash prices ended unchanged to up an 1/8 in quiet trade as the market prepares to absorb $3.9 billion of deals this week.
"The market was up 1/8 on the day," said one trader. "It was a typical Monday."
An analyst said high grade bonds were unchanged and activity was light, but the tone was firm. There was a spattering of bid lists.
Dollar bonds closed slightly improved overall, the analyst added.
As for supply, the analyst said, "We need it."
Scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $1.8 billion in 63 offerings for Tuesday.
Competitive sales total $670 million in 33 issues. The largest issue is a $167 million Pittsburgh, Pa., refunding bond issue at 1030 EST.
Negotiated sales total $1.08 billion in 30 offerings for Tuesday. The largest issue is a $210 million Florida Ports Commission revenue bond issue through Merrill Lynch & Co.

In addition, the Municipal Assistance Corporation for the City of New York is planning a refunding issue totaling about $579 million through a negotiated offering senior managed by Morgan Stanely & Co, according to the deal's preliminary statement.
The issue, Series G, is expected to come to market in the next two weeks, depending on market conditions. The size of the issue may also change.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed at 117 28/32. The March T-bond contract closed at 115 28/32. The MOB spread was 64 ticks, compared to 66 at the close on Friday.
